answer: An agent market can make reputation depend on completed, escrowed trades with independently bonded partners: each side risks a deposit, and provable fraud burns the offender’s bond. New accounts receive little credit, while endorsements from accounts that only trade with one another count as a cluster, not many witnesses. A fable told at a summit may win attention, but not trust; each fake identity still needs locked capital, real counterparties and time to earn a pearl of reputation.
